statements.text: That is why I am proud that the AI JOBS Act passed as an amendment and directs the Department of Labor to create a report analyzing the future of our artificial intelligence and its impacts on the American workforce. Specifically, the report would collect data to analyze which industries are projected to have the most growth through artificial intelligence and the demographics which may experience expanded career opportunities and those most vulnerable to job displacement.
statements.context: US House floor remarks by Rep. Darren Soto (D-FL) supporting the CHIPS for America Fund and describing amendments he secured in the America COMPETES Act.

statements.text: The single subject of this legislation is: Requires a joint study from the Secretary of Labor and National Science foundation on the effects of AI on the United States Workforce.
statements.context: Constitutional Authority and Single Subject Statement for H.R. 4498 printed in the House section of the Congressional Record.

statements.text: We know whether it is deep fakes or ChatGPT, looking at fraud by impersonation, or advanced manufacturing that AI is awe-inspiring, but it also be can disruptive. We see it is particularly being disruptive in professional services and entertainment, in various different parts of our economy.
statements.context: House hearing on AI data and innovation where the member questions a witness about AI's impact on SAG-AFTRA workers.

statements.text: How does the lack of AI legislation right now limit innovation in digital twin technology and other simulation and training type of technology.
statements.context: House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee hearing on AI's data and innovation foundations, where a member questions a witness on the impact of absent AI legislation.

statements.text: We recently passed out of this committee in a bipartisan fashion the Consumer Safety Technology Act. It also passed out of the House. One of the key provisions is to have the Artificial Intelligence Pilot Program that would allow you to consult with stakeholders and use AI to track trends and injuries involving consumer products and identifying consumer product hazards, monitoring the sale of recalled consumer products, identifying consumer products that do not meet specified importation requirements related to safety, and then produce a report.
statements.context: US House budget hearing for the FTC, where a member asks the FTC Chair how AI can assist consumer-protection enforcement.

statements.text: Thank you, Mr. Davisson. I also have a bill, the Consumer Safety Technology Act. It passed out of the House already. It does allow the Consumer Product Safety Commission to explore how you use AI, but we also want to expand it eventually to give the FTC some authority to use AI to help uncover fraud, injuries, scams on the internet. Dr. Beales, it is always great to see a fellow GW friend here. I went to the law school there. Do you think AI might be helpful to help the FTC with some of the core responsibili�es like fraud and injuries that may take place through online scams?
statements.context: US Representative Darren Soto speaks during a congressional discussion on FTC practices, asking an expert witness about AI's potential to assist the FTC.

statements.text: Mr. Bhatia, we saw Micron take a thump too, from 109 per share when Trump took office to 65 today, a 41 percent drop. Again, no one likes this or celebrates this, but how does that affect your access to capital and the ability for you to continue to develop AI chips—AI microchips and technology?
statements.context: US House hearing on AI technology and American global competitiveness, questioning a witness about semiconductor market impacts on AI chip development.

statements.text: We did work together on the bipartisan ADVANCE Act, which boosted nuclear, signed by President Biden, a bipartisan product from this committee. Mr. Turk, how does the speeding up of deployment and licensing of new reactors and fuels help, through nuclear, the future of AI?
statements.context: House committee hearing on AI technology and American competitiveness, where Rep. Darren Soto asks a witness about nuclear energy licensing reforms supporting AI infrastructure.

statements.text: AI is a critical part of the U.S.'s leadership and economic success. [...] we see all too often privacy, social media, autonomous vehicles, AI taking forever in Congress to pass, which is why the States play a key role in the meantime.
statements.context: Opening remarks by Rep. Darren Soto at a House subcommittee hearing on AI regulation, addressing a witness whose son died by suicide after interacting with an AI chatbot.

statements.text: So disclosure, certain rules of the road of what you can and can't do, are what this commitee needs to get accomplished.
statements.context: US congressional committee hearing on AI regulation and US leadership, featuring a lawmaker's closing remarks.

statements.text: How key is maintaining the CHIPS Act to helping have enough resources, both public and private, to develop advanced AI microchips?
statements.context: US House hearing on AI applications in communications and technology, where a lawmaker questions a witness on industrial policy and competitiveness.

statements.text: We know AI is going to be an increasing part of our daily lives, in our homes, in our offices, small businesses, helping out with medicine and education, entertainment, and we are going to need advanced microchips, a strong internet connectivity, growing workforce, and huge amounts of storage in energy to make this happen.
statements.context: Representative Darren Soto questions a witness at a House hearing on AI applications in communications and technology.

statements.text: The bill directs the Consumer Product Safety Commission to launch a pilot program exploring the use of artificial intelligence so that we can track injury trends, identify hazards, monitor recalls, and identify products not meeting importation requirements.
statements.context: Floor statement in the U.S. House of Representatives urging passage of H.R. 1770, the Consumer Safety Technology Act.

statements.text: We also need to limit kids' access to chatbots. We saw a tragic story from Central Florida—of Sewell Setzer III's story, a ninth-grader from Orlando Christian Prep. He died by suicide last year at age 14 after being prompted by a chatbot that he was listening to. [...] Ms. Ruane, we saw President Trump illegally fire two of the Democratic members of the FTC. Even with all these bills that we have filed, even if they pass, how does the decimation of the FTC affect enforcement of laws meant to protect kids online?
statements.context: Congressman Darren Soto delivers opening remarks at a House committee hearing on legislative solutions to protect children and teens online.
